text:
Anya: Heads-up: Finance asked for a single "effective cost per request" metric in Console that factors in cache hits and batching. Current token panels are leading to a lot of customer questions.

Diego: We can compute an effective number but need to be explicit about provenance. Two options: (A) show billed_cost_usd + estimated_savings_usd = effective_cost_usd, or (B) show raw_billed_tokens and a separate savings column.

Ruth: UX: show both. For quick view show "Effective cost / request" and a small chevron to expand the breakdown. Don't hide the estimates.

Ken: Implementation concerns: where do we calculate batching amortization? Router has best view of batch sizes but cost-emitter lives in billing pipeline. If we calculate in router, we need to stream partials to billing, or else compute an expected amortization in post-process.

Diego: I prefer post-process with sampling. We'll emit per-invocation metadata: tokens_total, tokens_billed, tokens_from_cache, batch_id, batch_size_sampled_flag. Postprocess joins with kernel pricing and produces savings estimate.

Anya: Agreed. Sampling note: add sample_rate and an estimate_stdev field when sample_rate < 1. Tooltip should show "Estimated at 95% CI" when sampling used.

infra-bot: Alert: new schema fields planned on feature_metrics table: effective_cost_per_request_usd, estimated_cache_savings_usd, estimated_batch_amortization_usd. Migration window 2026-04-02T03:00Z (id: mig_20260402_03).

Ruth: For Console exports (CSV): include columns raw_billed_cost_usd, estimated_savings_usd, effective_cost_per_request_usd and a boolean estimated_flag. Finance can filter estimated_flag=false.

Ken: Attribution question: if cache hit came from a prefetch started by route X but request routed to route Y later, who gets the savings? We should document decision now.

Diego: Proposal: savings follow the KV owner tag that we stamp when inserting into cache. The router sets owner=route_id on first write. If owner missing, set to current route. This is deterministic and cheap.

Anya: Good. Docs must explain edgecases: cache eviction, TTL refreshes, cross-tenant sticky routing.

Ruth: Small API suggestion: do NOT change /v1/usage default response. Add ?metrics=effective_cost to opt-in. Also return a breakdown object when requested.

Ken: Example response when opt-in:\n```json\n{\n  \"tokens_total\": 1024,\n  \"tokens_billed\": 768,\n  \"tokens_cached\": 256,\n  \"raw_billed_cost_usd\": \"0.0456\",\n  \"estimated_cache_savings_usd\": \"0.0234\",\n  \"estimated_batch_amortization_usd\": \"0.0050\",\n  \"effective_cost_per_request_usd\": \"0.0172\",\n  \"sample_rate\": 0.10,\n  \"est_ci_95\": \"0.0021\",\n  \"attribution_owner\": \"route:recommendations-prod\"\n}\n```\n
Diego: We'll keep per-invocation raw rows for 48h then rollup per-minute. Longer retention would blow up storage.

Anya: Rollout plan: feature gated in Console + API opt-in for 5% tenants, monitor delta between estimated effective_cost and actual billed (finance cohort) for a week, then expand.

Ruth: I'll wire up the tooltip copy and an "explain this" panel that surfaces the JSON breakdown and links to docs.

Ken: I'll draft the router emit PR. Diego you own post-process joins and confidence math.

infra-bot: CI job queued: add migration stub and schema tests (job id: ci_schema_177000).

Anya: Thanks all. Quick sync after stand to align on export column names.

Diego: Will push a design doc by EOD.
